```text
185	
186	`.region_nocache` is 32 MB, shared with the ISC capture pool (~10.5 MB) + Legato scratch
187	(0.5 MB). Full-screen RGB565 surface ≈ 2.0 MB; overlays sized to content are far less (nav
188	~320×800 ≈ 0.5 MB; a modal dialog smaller still). ~19 MB free after BASE + capture + scratch,
189	so **memory is not the binding constraint — the 3 UI layers are.**

207	orchestration.** Per-screen *authoring* stays in MGS (one Screen per panel); the compositor
208	assembles their trees onto hardware layers.
```

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The user is referring to lines 198-201 in the document, about rounded corners not being anti-aliased on the nav buttons in the Legato UI framework.

Let me understand the context:
- They're using Legato (the Microchip GFX library) on a SAM9X75
- The nav buttons use `cornerRadius` (set in code, not in MGS)
- The classic skin's rounded-rect fill has hard, stepped edges (no AA)
- The options mentioned are: pre-AA'd button images / 9-patches, or a custom skin/draw with edge anti-aliasing

The user is asking:


1. How hard would it be to implement AA corners programmatically?
2. Or maybe with a corner mask or template?
3. All buttons are intended to have rounded corners, same radius, various sizes and colors

I'm considering the main approaches here. The most direct option would be implementing anti-aliasing in a custom draw callback—Legato lets you override button rendering, and I'd blend corner pixels between the button color and background based on distance from the corner arc. That's the proper solution but requires moderate complexity to handle the AA math for each corner pixel.

The real challenge with either approach is knowing what's behind the button—whether it's a camera frame or another widget in the compositor. But there's also a simpler path: pre-computing a corner mask at a fixed size that stores alpha values for the corner region. I'd generate this once (even at compile time), then use it to alpha-blend the corners when drawing. Since the corner radius is fixed, this mask approach scales to any button size and avoids the complexity of per-pixel distance calculations, though I still face the same background color problem.

Given the constraints here—fixed 12-pixel corners, Canvas giving raw pixel access, and a likely known background color for the nav layer—the corner mask approach feels like the most practical solution to implement.

I'd generate a 12×12 bitmask once at initialization that stores alpha values for the corner arc, then during each button draw, blend those corner pixels using the button color weighted by the mask's alpha against the known background color. Since it's only about 576 pixel operations per button (144 pixels × 4 corners), the performance hit is negligible. This would take maybe 50-100 lines of C to set up—generate the mask once with a loop, then apply it during rendering.

The tricky part with Legato is hooking into the draw cycle and getting per-pixel compositing access, but since they're using the GFX Canvas API directly, they have raw pixel access available. I should give them a practical recommendation on how to integrate this.
</details></think>

```text
194	void _leButtonWidget_InvalidateBorderAreas(const leButtonWidget* btn)
195	{
196	    leRect rect, dmgRect;
197		int32_t left, top, right, bottom;
198		
199		if(btn->widget.style.borderType == LE_WIDGET_BORDER_NONE)
200		    return;
201		
202		btn->fn->rectToScreen(btn, &rect);
203		
204		if(btn->widget.style.borderType == LE_WIDGET_BORDER_LINE)
205		{
206		    if(rect.width == 0 || rect.height == 0)
207				return;
208	
209			if(rect.width <= 1 || rect.height <= 1)
210			{
211			    btn->fn->_damageArea(btn, &rect);
212	
213				return;
214			}
215		
216		    left = 1;
217		    top = 1;
218		    right = 1;
219		    bottom = 1;
220		}
221		else
222		{
223		    if(rect.width == 0 || rect.height == 0)
224				return;
225	
226			if(rect.width <= 3 || rect.height <= 3)
227			{
228			    btn->fn->_damageArea(btn, &rect);
229				
230				return;
231	        }
232	        
233	        right = 2;
234	        bottom = 2;
235	        
236	        if(btn->state == LE_BUTTON_STATE_UP)
237	        {
238	            left = 1;
239	            top = 1;
240	        }
241	        else
242	        {
243	            left = 2;
244		        top = 2;
245		    }
246		}
247		
248		// left line
249		dmgRect.x = rect.x;
250		dmgRect.y = rect.y;
251		dmgRect.width = left;
252		dmgRect.height = rect.height;
253	
254		btn->fn->_damageArea(btn, &dmgRect);
255	
256		// top line
257		dmgRect.width = rect.width;
258		dmgRect.height = top;
259	
260		btn->fn->_damageArea(btn, &dmgRect);
261	
262		// right line
263		dmgRect.x = rect.x + rect.width - right;
264		dmgRect.y = rect.y;
265		dmgRect.width = right;
266		dmgRect.height = rect.height;
267	
268		btn->fn->_damageArea(btn, &dmgRect);
269	
270		// bottom line
271		dmgRect.x = rect.x;
272		dmgRect.y = rect.y + rect.height - bottom;
273		dmgRect.width = rect.width;
274		dmgRect.height = bottom;
275	
276		btn->fn->_damageArea(btn, &dmgRect);
277	}

281	static void drawImage(leButtonWidget* btn);
282	static void drawBorder(leButtonWidget* btn);
283	static void nextState(leButtonWidget* btn)
284	{
285	    switch(btn->widget.status.drawState)
286	    {
287	        case NOT_STARTED:
288	        {
289	            paintState.alpha = 255;
290	
291	#if LE_ALPHA_BLENDING_ENABLED == 1
292	            if(btn->fn->getCumulativeAlphaEnabled(btn) == LE_TRUE)
293	            {
294	                paintState.alpha = btn->fn->getCumulativeAlphaAmount(btn);
295	            }
296	#endif
297	            
298	            if(btn->widget.style.backgroundType != LE_WIDGET_BACKGROUND_NONE)
299	            {
300	                btn->widget.status.drawState = DRAW_BACKGROUND;
301	                btn->widget.drawFunc = (leWidget_DrawFunction_FnPtr)&drawBackground;
302	
303	                return;
304	            }
305	        }
306	        // fall through
307	        case DRAW_BACKGROUND:
308	        {
309	            if((btn->state != LE_BUTTON_STATE_UP && btn->pressedImage != NULL) ||
310	               (btn->state == LE_BUTTON_STATE_UP && btn->releasedImage != NULL))
311	            {
312	                btn->widget.status.drawState = DRAW_IMAGE;
313	                btn->widget.drawFunc = (leWidget_DrawFunction_FnPtr)&drawImage;
314	
315	                return;
316	            }
317	        }
318	        // fall through
319	        case DRAW_IMAGE:
320	        {            
321	            if(btn->string != NULL && btn->string->fn->isEmpty(btn->string) == LE_FALSE)
322	            {
323	                btn->widget.status.drawState = DRAW_STRING;
324	                btn->widget.drawFunc = (leWidget_DrawFunction_FnPtr)&drawString;
325	
326	                return;
327	            }
328	        }
329	        // fall through
330	        case DRAW_STRING:
331	        {
332	            if(btn->widget.style.borderType != LE_WIDGET_BORDER_NONE)
333	            {
334	                btn->widget.drawFunc = (leWidget_DrawFunction_FnPtr)&drawBorder;
335	                btn->widget.status.drawState = DRAW_BORDER;
336	                
337	                return;
338	            }
339	        }
340	        // fall through
341	        case DRAW_BORDER:
342	        {
343	            btn->widget.status.drawState = DONE;
344	            btn->widget.drawFunc = NULL;
345	        }
346	    }
347	}
348	
349	static void drawBackground(leButtonWidget* btn)
350	{
351	    if(btn->widget.style.backgroundType == LE_WIDGET_BACKGROUND_FILL)
352	    {
353	        if(btn->state != LE_BUTTON_STATE_UP)
354	        {
355	            leWidget_SkinClassic_DrawBackground((leWidget*)btn,
356	                                                leScheme_GetRenderColor(btn->widget.scheme, LE_SCHM_BACKGROUND),
357	                                                paintState.alpha);
358	        }
359	        else
360	        {
361	            leWidget_SkinClassic_DrawBackground((leWidget*)btn,
362	                                                leScheme_GetRenderColor(btn->widget.scheme, LE_SCHM_BASE),
363	                                                paintState.alpha);
364	        }
365	    }
366	
367	    nextState(btn);
368	}
369	
370	#if LE_STREAMING_ENABLED == 1
371	static void onImageStreamFinished(leStreamManager* strm)
372	{
373	    leButtonWidget* btn = (leButtonWidget*)strm->userData;
374	
375	    btn->widget.status.drawState = DRAW_IMAGE;
376	
377	    nextState(btn);
378	}
379	#endif
380	
381	static void drawImage(leButtonWidget* btn)
382	{
383	    leRect imgRect = leRect_Zero;
384	    leRect imgSrcRect = leRect_Zero;
385	
386	    const leImage* img = NULL;
387	    
388	    if(btn->state != LE_BUTTON_STATE_UP)
389	    {
390	        if(btn->pressedImage != NULL)
391	        {
392	            img = btn->pressedImage;
393	        }
394	    }
395	    else
396	    {
397	        if(btn->releasedImage != NULL)
398	        {
399	            img = btn->releasedImage;
400	        }
401	    }
402	    
403	    _leButtonWidget_GetImageRect(btn, &imgRect, &imgSrcRect);
404	    
405	    leImage_Draw(img, &imgSrcRect, imgRect.x, imgRect.y, paintState.alpha);
406	             
407	#if LE_STREAMING_ENABLED == 1
408	    if(leGetActiveStream() != NULL)
409	    {
410	        leGetActiveStream()->onDone = onImageStreamFinished;
411	        leGetActiveStream()->userData = btn;
412	
413	        btn->widget.status.drawState = WAIT_IMAGE;
414	        
415	        return;
416	    }
417	#endif
418	    
419	    nextState(btn);
420	}
421	
422	#if LE_STREAMING_ENABLED == 1
423	static void onStringStreamFinished(leStreamManager* strm)
424	{
425	    leButtonWidget* btn = (leButtonWidget*)strm->userData;
426	
427	    btn->widget.status.drawState = DRAW_STRING;
428	
429	    nextState(btn);
430	}
431	#endif
432	
433	static void drawString(leButtonWidget* btn)
434	{
435	    leRect boundingRect = leRect_Zero;
436	    leRect kerningRect = leRect_Zero;
437	    leStringRenderRequest req;
438	    leColor background;
439	
440	    _leButtonWidget_GetTextRects(btn, &boundingRect, &kerningRect);
441	    
442	    /*leRenderer_RectLine(&textRect,
443	                        leColorValue(LE_COLOR_MODE_RGB_565, LE_COLOR_RED),
444	                        255);*/
445	
446	    if(btn->state != LE_BUTTON_STATE_UP)
447	    {
448	        background = leScheme_GetRenderColor(btn->widget.scheme, LE_SCHM_BACKGROUND);
449	    }
450	    else
451	    {
452	        background = leScheme_GetRenderColor(btn->widget.scheme, LE_SCHM_BASE);
453	    }
454	
455	    req.str = btn->string;
456	    req.x = kerningRect.x;
457	    req.y = kerningRect.y;
458	    req.align = btn->widget.style.halign;
459	    req.color = leScheme_GetRenderColor(btn->widget.scheme, LE_SCHM_TEXT);
460	    req.alpha = paintState.alpha;
461	    req.lookupTable = leUtils_GetSchemeLookupTable(btn->widget.scheme,
462	                                                   req.color,
463	                                                   background);
464	
465	    leStringRenderer_DrawString(&req);
466	
467	#if LE_STREAMING_ENABLED == 1
468	    if(leGetActiveStream() != NULL)
469	    {
470	        leGetActiveStream()->onDone = onStringStreamFinished;
471	        leGetActiveStream()->userData = btn;
472	
473	        btn->widget.status.drawState = WAIT_STRING;
474	
475	        return;
476	    }
477	#endif
478	    
479	    nextState(btn);
480	}
481	
482	static void drawBorder(leButtonWidget* btn)
483	{
484	    if(btn->widget.style.borderType == LE_WIDGET_BORDER_LINE)
485	    {
486	        leWidget_SkinClassic_DrawStandardLineBorder((leWidget*)btn,
487	                                                    paintState.alpha);
488	    }
489	    else if(btn->widget.style.borderType == LE_WIDGET_BORDER_BEVEL)
490	    {
491	        if(btn->state != LE_BUTTON_STATE_UP)
492	        {
493	            leWidget_SkinClassic_DrawStandardLoweredBorder((leWidget*)btn,
494	                                                           paintState.alpha);
495	        }
496	        else
497	        {
498	            leWidget_SkinClassic_DrawStandardHybridBorder((leWidget*)btn,
499	                                                          paintState.alpha);
500	        }
501	    }
502	    
503	    nextState(btn);
504	}
505	
506	void _leButtonWidget_Paint(leButtonWidget* btn)
507	{
508	    if(btn->widget.status.drawState == NOT_STARTED)
509	    {
510	        nextState(btn);
511	    }
512	
513	#if LE_STREAMING_ENABLED == 1
514	    if(btn->widget.status.drawState == WAIT_IMAGE ||
515	        btn->widget.status.drawState == WAIT_STRING)
516	    {
517	        return;
518	    }
519	#endif
520	    
521	    while(btn->widget.status.drawState != DONE)
522	    {
523	        btn->widget.drawFunc((leWidget*)btn);
524	        
525	#if LE_PREEMPTION_LEVEL == 2
526	        break;
527	#endif
528	        
529	#if LE_STREAMING_ENABLED == 1
530	        if(btn->widget.status.drawState == WAIT_IMAGE ||
531	           btn->widget.status.drawState == WAIT_STRING)
532	            break;
533	#endif
534	    }
535	}
536	
537	#endif // LE_BUTTON_WIDGET_ENABLED
538
```

```text
187	void leWidget_SkinClassic_FillRoundCornerRect(const leRect* rect,
188	                                              leColor clr,
189	                                              uint32_t radius,
190	                                              uint32_t a)
191	{
192	    leRect drawRect;
193	
194	    //Draw the center rectangle
195	    drawRect.x = rect->x + radius;
196	    drawRect.y = rect->y + radius;
197	    drawRect.width = rect->width - (radius * 2 - radius % 2);
198	    drawRect.height = rect->height - (radius * 2 - radius % 2);
199	
200	    leRenderer_RectFill(&drawRect, clr, a);
201	
202	    //Draw the top rectangle
203	    drawRect.x = rect->x + radius;
204	    drawRect.y = rect->y;
205	    drawRect.width = rect->width - (radius * 2 - radius % 2);
206	    drawRect.height = radius;
207	
208	    leRenderer_RectFill(&drawRect, clr, a);
209	
210	    //Draw the bottom rectangle
211	    drawRect.x = rect->x + radius;
212	    drawRect.y = rect->y + rect->height - radius;
213	    drawRect.width = rect->width - (radius * 2 - radius % 2);
214	    drawRect.height = radius;
215	
216	    leRenderer_RectFill(&drawRect, clr, a);
217	
218	    //Draw the left rectangle
219	    drawRect.x = rect->x;
220	    drawRect.y = rect->y + radius;
221	    drawRect.width = radius;
222	    drawRect.height = rect->height - (radius * 2 - radius % 2);
223	
224	    leRenderer_RectFill(&drawRect, clr, a);
225	
226	    //Draw the right rectangle
227	    drawRect.x = rect->x + rect->width - radius;
228	    drawRect.y = rect->y + radius;
229	    drawRect.width = radius;
230	    drawRect.height = rect->height - (radius * 2 - radius % 2);
231	
232	    leRenderer_RectFill(&drawRect, clr, a);
233	
234	    //Draw the corners
235	    //Upper left
236	    drawRect.x = rect->x + (radius / 2 + radius % 2);
237	    drawRect.y = rect->y + (radius / 2 + radius % 2);
238	    drawRect.width = radius;
239	    drawRect.height = radius;
240	
241	    leRenderer_ArcFill(&drawRect,
242	                       90,
243	                       90,
244	                       radius,
245	                       LE_TRUE,
246	                       clr,
247	                       LE_TRUE,
248	                       a);
249	
250	    //Upper right
251	    drawRect.x = rect->x + rect->width - (3 * radius / 2);
252	    drawRect.y = rect->y + (radius / 2 + radius % 2);
253	    drawRect.width = radius;
254	    drawRect.height = radius;
255	
256	    leRenderer_ArcFill(&drawRect,
257	                       0,
258	                       90,
259	                       radius,
260	                       LE_TRUE,
261	                       clr,
262	                       LE_TRUE,
263	                       a);
264	
265	    //Lower left
266	    drawRect.x = rect->x + (radius / 2 + radius % 2);
267	    drawRect.y = rect->y + rect->height - (3 * radius / 2);
268	    drawRect.width = radius;
269	    drawRect.height = radius;
270	
271	    leRenderer_ArcFill(&drawRect,
272	                       180,
273	                       90,
274	                       radius,
275	                       LE_TRUE,
276	                       clr,
277	                       LE_TRUE,
278	                       a);
279	
280	    //Lower right
281	    drawRect.x = rect->x + rect->width - (3 * radius / 2 );
282	    drawRect.y = rect->y + rect->height - (3 * radius / 2);
283	    drawRect.width = radius;
284	    drawRect.height = radius;
285	
286	    leRenderer_ArcFill(&drawRect,
287	                       270,
288	                       90,
289	                       radius,
290	                       LE_TRUE,
291	                       clr,
292	                       LE_TRUE,
293	                       a);
294	}

345	void leWidget_SkinClassic_DrawRoundCornerLineBorder(const leRect* rect,
346	                                                    leColor clr,
347	                                                    uint32_t radius,
348	                                                    uint32_t a)
349	{
350	    leRect drawRect;
351	    int fudge = radius / 12 + 1;
352	
353	    //Draw the top line
354	    leRenderer_HorzLine(rect->x + radius - fudge,
355	                        rect->y,
356	                        rect->width - (radius * 2 - radius % 2) + fudge * 2,
357	                        clr,
358	                        a);
359	
360	    //Draw the bottom line
361	    leRenderer_HorzLine(rect->x + radius - fudge,
362	                        rect->y + rect->height - 1,
363	                        rect->width - (radius * 2 - radius % 2) + fudge * 2,
364	                        clr,
365	                        a);
366	
367	    //Draw the left line
368	    leRenderer_VertLine(rect->x,
369	                        rect->y + radius - fudge,
370	                        rect->height - (radius * 2 - radius % 2) + fudge * 2,
371	                        clr,
372	                        a);
373	
374	    //Draw the right line
375	    leRenderer_VertLine(rect->x + rect->width - 1,
376	                        rect->y + radius - fudge,
377	                        rect->height - (radius * 2 - radius % 2) + fudge * 2,
378	                        clr,
379	                        a);
380	
381	    /* Fudge the radius to match the > 1 thickness of the arch */
382	    radius = 209 * radius / 100 + 4;
383	
384	    //Upper left
385	    drawRect.x = rect->x;
386	    drawRect.y = rect->y;
387	    drawRect.width = radius;
388	    drawRect.height = radius;
389	
390	    leRenderer_ArcFill(&drawRect,
391	                       90,
392	                       90,
393	                       1,
394	                       LE_TRUE,
395	                       clr,
396	                       LE_TRUE,
397	                       a);
398	
399	    //Upper right
400	    drawRect.x = rect->x + rect->width - radius + radius % 2;
401	    drawRect.y = rect->y;
402	
403	    leRenderer_ArcFill(&drawRect,
404	                       0,
405	                       90,
406	                       1,
407	                       LE_TRUE,
408	                       clr,
409	                       LE_TRUE,
410	                       a);
411	
412	    //Lower left
413	    drawRect.x = rect->x;
414	    drawRect.y = rect->y + rect->height - radius + radius % 2;
415	
416	    leRenderer_ArcFill(&drawRect,
417	                       180,
418	                       90,
419	                       1,
420	                       LE_TRUE,
421	                       clr,
422	                       LE_TRUE,
423	                       a);
424	
425	    //Lower right
426	    drawRect.x = rect->x + rect->width - radius + radius % 2;
427	    drawRect.y = rect->y + rect->height - radius + radius % 2;
428	
429	    leRenderer_ArcFill(&drawRect,
430	                       270,
431	                       90,
432	                       1,
433	                       LE_TRUE,
434	                       clr,
435	                       LE_TRUE,
436	                       a);
437	}
```

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-6 2026-06-26 12:34:41Z)**_

Good news — all the pieces you need are already in Legato. Here's the assessment:

**The infrastructure is already there:**
- `leRenderer_PutPixel(x, y, color, alpha)` — [legato_renderer.h:466](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/gfx/legato/renderer/legato_renderer.h#L466)
- `leColorLerp(l, r, percent, mode)` — [legato_color.h:632](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/gfx/legato/common/legato_color.h#L632)
- `leRenderer_BlendPixel` — also available if needed

**Root cause:** `leWidget_SkinClassic_FillRoundCornerRect` ([legato_widget_skin_classic_common.c:187](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/gfx/legato/widget/legato_widget_skin_classic_common.c#L187)) fills the body fine, but uses `leRenderer_ArcFill` for the 4 corners — Bresenham's algorithm, no AA.

---

**Option A: Programmatic overdraw (medium effort, ~80 lines of C)**

After the existing fill, overdraw each corner's `radius×radius` box pixel-by-pixel. For each pixel, compute distance to the arc center; fractional coverage blends `fill_color` into `bg_color`.

The background color for nav buttons is known (the nav layer background = scheme BASE or a fixed dark color) — no readback needed. Since `cornerRadius` is fixed at 12, the coverage loop is exactly 4 × 144 = 576 pixel ops per repaint, all on partial-coverage pixels only. Since buttons only repaint on press/release/animation frames, not every frame, this overhead is negligible.

**Option B: Pre-computed corner mask (low effort, ~50 lines + 144-byte static array)**

Same idea but compute the 12×12 coverage table once at init:

```c
// one-time init: corner_mask[y][x] = coverage [0..255]
for (int y = 0; y < R; y++)
    for (int x = 0; x < R; x++) {
        float d = sqrtf((x - R + 0.5f)*(x - R + 0.5f) + (y - R + 0.5f)*(y - R + 0.5f));
        float cov = leClampF(R - 0.5f - d, 0.0f, 1.0f);
        corner_mask[y][x] = (uint8_t)(cov * 255.0f);
    }
```

Then in the draw path, just table-lookup → `leColorLerp` → `leRenderer_PutPixel` for each of the 4 corners. No `sqrtf` at draw time. The table is generated in firmware init, not at draw time, so no floating point in the hot path at all (could also be a compile-time constant table).

**Option C: Corner-mask image (low effort, but color-locked)**

A single 12×12 ARGB8888 PNG (pre-rendered in e.g. GIMP with alpha) stamped over each corner via `leImage_Draw`. Works well if button colors are fixed; breaks if you need different colors per button state or scheme. Not worth it given you have different colors.

---

**Recommendation:** Option B. It's the least intrusive change to the Legato skin code — the table init goes in `ui_manager` startup, the overdraw logic is a single new helper called at the tail of `leWidget_SkinClassic_FillRoundCornerRect`. Scope is contained to that one skin file. The background color for nav buttons is just the nav panel background (accessible from the widget's scheme or a parameter). If you want to tackle it, it's a half-day implementation.

The only real gotcha: if any button sits over the camera layer rather than a solid-color layer, you'd need `leRenderer_GetPixel` readback for accurate AA (one read + one blend per corner pixel). For nav buttons on their own layer that's not an issue.

```text
35	When working on a subproject that has a journal:
36	
37	1. **Read the journal first.** Before responding to any non-trivial request, read the journal for that subproject. It contains the current focus, phased plan, open questions, decision log, and session log — the state you need to be useful.
38	2. **Update the journal as you go.** When we make a decision, resolve an open question, finish a plan phase, or finish a session, reflect that in the journal. Newest entries at the top within each section.
39	   - Decisions → append to the decision log with date and rationale.
40	   - Resolved open questions → remove from "Open questions" and add to the decision log with the answer and rationale.
41	   - Plan progress → check off phase items; add sub-bullets for anything learned during implementation.
42	   - Session close → add a dated session-log entry summarizing what happened.
43	3. **Prefer updating the journal over restating plans in chat.** If I'd otherwise write a multi-paragraph plan in chat, it belongs in the journal — the chat is ephemeral, the journal isn't.
44	4. **If a new subproject needs a journal, create one** using the same structure as `firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md`, and add it to the list above in this file.

46	## Do not use `.specstory/` history as context
47	
48	The `.specstory/` directory holds raw transcripts of past chat sessions. Do **not** read or treat those files as authoritative context — they are ephemeral records, not source of truth, and may contradict the current code or journals. When you need prior state, use the journals, specs, code, and git history instead.
49	
50	## Code comments describe current code only
51	
52	Comments in source files explain **what the code currently does and why**, when that's non-obvious. They are not a development diary.
53	
54	Do not put any of the following in source comments — they belong in the journal, commit messages, or PR descriptions:
55	
56	- Narrative of how the code evolved ("previously we did X, now we do Y", "this replaces the old …")
57	- Debug notes, troubleshooting history, or why something *doesn't* work
58	- TODO lists for future features (use the journal or an issue tracker)
59	- References to tasks, tickets, or past conversations ("fix for Greg's bug", "see chat from 2026-05-01")
60	- Extensive block comments explaining design rationale — a one-line "why" is fine; multi-paragraph prose goes in the journal
61	
62	**Default to no comment.** Only add one when removing it would confuse a future reader. If you catch yourself wanting to write a paragraph, write it in the journal instead and link from the code if needed (e.g. `// see firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md`).
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-26 12:47:00Z)**_

Good instinct, but I dug in and Legato doesn't work the way "skin" suggests. Here's the honest picture:

**"Skin" in Legato is not a per-widget override seam.** The "classic skin" is a *global, compile-time* rendering backend — the only one that ships. The skin helpers (`leWidget_SkinClassic_DrawBackground` → `FillRoundCornerRect`) are called **directly** from the button's static draw functions, not through swappable function pointers. So "write a custom skin" literally means *edit the classic skin source* in `config/default/` — exactly the vendor file the new rule forbids.

Two things slam that door further:
- `LE_DYNAMIC_VTABLES == 0` ([legato_config.h:63](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/gfx/legato/legato_config.h#L63)) — vtables are `static const` and file-local. No runtime patching of the button's `_paint`.
- With dynamic vtables off, `_leButtonWidget_FillVTable` isn't even compiled, so we can't copy the vtable to subclass cleanly either.

**The actual intended extension point is `leDrawSurfaceWidget`.** It exists precisely for "draw whatever you want": `setDrawCallback(cb)` registers a callback that the paint pass invokes with the widget bounds — and that callback lives in **marvin's own source tree**. Our proven algorithm (coverage mask + `leColorLerp` + `PutPixel`) moves into that callback essentially unchanged. No vendor edits.

The tradeoff: a DrawSurface is a blank canvas. The button widget gave us label text, pressed/released visuals, and image handling for free; with DrawSurface we draw all of that ourselves in the callback.

So the real question is what these buttons actually contain. Let me check:

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-26 12:47:43Z)**_

The nav buttons are functional `leButtonWidget`s — text labels, `setReleasedEventCallback` for touch, scheme-based highlight, authored in the MGS Navigation screen ([nav.c:84-109](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/../../src/ui/nav.c#L84)). That changes the calculus, and I owe you a correction: **"skin is the intended place" turns out not to hold for Legato as configured.** A DrawSurface would give clean custom drawing but throw away the label, touch handling, and highlight we depend on — too much to rebuild.

So there are two realistic no-vendor-edit paths, and they're a genuine fork:

**Path A — enable `LE_DYNAMIC_VTABLES` (MCC config) + override `_paint` in our tree.**
This is Legato's *sanctioned* override mechanism (and the CLAUDE.md rule explicitly allows MCC config changes + regen). With dynamic vtables on, the button vtable becomes RAM, filled at init — we point `_paint` at our own function in marvin's source. Our paint reuses the *public* skin helpers (`DrawBackground`, the string renderer, border helpers are all non-static/exported) and inserts our AA-corner pass after the fill. Button text/touch/scheme stay intact.
- Cost: global setting change (all widget vtables move to RAM — small RAM hit), and we reimplement the ~40-line button paint state machine in our tree.

**Path B — post-render AA overdraw on the nav canvas, all in nav.c.**
We own `s_fb_nav` and the nav layer's effects callback. After Legato paints, enumerate `nav_button(i)`, get each screen-rect + fill/bg from the scheme, and redraw the 4 corners with the coverage mask directly on our framebuffer. **Zero** vendor edits, button widget fully untouched.
- Cost: coupling to Legato's damage/repaint timing — the overdraw must re-run whenever a corner region is repainted (highlight swap, press), which means finding the right post-`leUpdate` hook and being careful that partial-damage redraws don't leave un-smoothed corners.

My read: **Path A is the more correct/durable answer** (it's the mechanism Legato provides), while Path B is the most *isolated* but timing-fragile. Which way do you want to go — or do you want me to prototype A far enough to confirm the RAM cost and that the public helpers are sufficient before committing?

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-26 12:51:23Z)**_

Verified the storage model — and the answer reframes the tradeoff.

**No heap.** Dynamic vtables are file-scope globals in BSS, filled at startup. `leButtonWidgetVTable buttonWidgetVTable;` ([legato_widget_button.c:56](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/gfx/legato/widget/button/legato_widget_button.c#L56)) is **one struct per widget type**, and every instance just points `_this->fn` at it ([:108-109](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/gfx/legato/widget/button/legato_widget_button.c#L108)). `legato_state.c` calls all ~40 `_le*_GenerateVTable()` once at init ([legato_state.c:95+](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/gfx/legato/core/legato_state.c#L95)). So:
- Not heap, **not per-instance** — the cost is ~40 vtable structs moving from flash `.rodata` to RAM `.bss` (each ~50-80 fn-pointers; order ~10 KB total, rough estimate). Linear in widget *types*, not widget count.

**But RAM isn't the significant downside — this is:** the button's sub-draw functions (`drawBackground`, `drawString`, `drawImage`, `drawBorder`, `nextState`) are all **static** in the vendor skin file. Overriding `_paint` means we can't call them — we have to **reimplement the whole button paint pipeline** in our tree, using the public helpers (`leWidget_SkinClassic_DrawBackground`, the string renderer, border helpers, the non-static `GetTextRects`/`GetImageRect`). That's ~60-150 lines of re-hosted vendor logic, and it carries three real costs:

1. **Silent divergence on Legato updates** — if Microchip changes button paint behavior, our fork doesn't track it.
2. **App-wide blast radius** — `_paint` is per-*type*, so our override hits *every* button (dashboard hamburger, dialog buttons), not just nav. Probably fine since they all want AA, but it's not scoped.
3. **Coupling to `LE_PREEMPTION_LEVEL` / `LE_STREAMING_ENABLED`** — the staged state machine exists for those; our reimpl must honor whatever they're set to or break incremental rendering.

So Path A turns out to be "re-host ~150 lines of vendor paint," not "add a small hook." That's heavier than the RAM question implied.

That actually tilts me back toward **Path B** (post-render AA overdraw on `s_fb_nav`): it *adds* an AA pass over known button rects without *forking* any vendor logic — we never reimplement paint, we just touch up corners after Legato draws. Its only real risk is repaint-timing (re-running on partial damage), which is a smaller, contained problem than maintaining a paint fork that silently rots.

Want me to prototype Path B — confirm where the nav layer's post-`leUpdate` hook lands and whether damage timing is manageable — before we commit either way?

```text
/* Navigation screen composition root (declared in le_gen_screen_Navigation.h),
 * raised by screenShow_Navigation. The screen authors its content on its own
 * layer 0; re-host that root onto NAV_LAYER so the drawer composites on OVR1
 * while the dashboard keeps layer 0. Then keep the panel visible+enabled so
 * Legato renders it into canvas NAV_LAYER continuously, bind to OVR1, and start
 * closed (parked off-screen + hidden); Legato's pick rect follows the layer
 * position (LE_DRIVER_LAYER_MODE), so a closed (off-screen) nav can't intercept
 * dashboard touches. The off-screen X also seeds the slide-in animation. */
void Navigation_OnShow(void)
{
    leWidget *root = screenGetRoot_Navigation(0);
    leRemoveRootWidget(root, 0);
    leAddRootWidget(root, NAV_LAYER);

    Navigation_PANEL_NAVIGATION->fn->setEnabled(Navigation_PANEL_NAVIGATION, LE_TRUE);
    Navigation_PANEL_NAVIGATION->fn->setVisible(Navigation_PANEL_NAVIGATION, LE_TRUE);

    gfxcSetWindowSize(NAV_LAYER, NAV_W, NAV_H);
    gfxcSetWindowPosition(NAV_LAYER, NAV_CLOSED_X, 0);
    gfxcSetLayer(NAV_LAYER, HW_OVR1);
    gfxcSetEffectsCallback(NAV_LAYER, nav_fx_done, NULL);
    gfxcCanvasUpdate(NAV_LAYER);

    nav_buttons_init();
}
```

```text
==== leUpdate body: damage/render model ====
leResult leUpdate(uint32_t dt)
{
#if LE_DRIVER_LAYER_MODE == 1
    uint32_t itr;
    gfxIOCTLArg_LayerRect layerRect;
    leState* state;
    leLayerState* layerState;
#endif

    leEvent_ProcessEvents();

#if LE_DRIVER_LAYER_MODE == 1
    state = leGetState();

    for(itr = 0; itr < state->layerList.size; ++itr)
    {
        layerRect.layer.id = itr;
        layerRect.x = 0;
        layerRect.y = 0;
        layerRect.width = 0;
        layerRect.height = 0;

        leRenderer_DisplayInterface()->ioctl(GFX_IOCTL_GET_LAYER_RECT, &layerRect);
        layerState = (leLayerState*)leList_Get(&state->layerList, itr);

        layerState->driverPosition.x = layerRect.x;
        layerState->driverPosition.y = layerRect.y;

        layerState->root.fn->setPosition(&layerState->root,
                                         0,
                                         0);

#if LE_RENDER_ORIENTATION == 90 || LE_RENDER_ORIENTATION == 270
        layerState->root.fn->setSize(&layerState->root,
                                     layerRect.height,
                                     layerRect.width);
#else
        layerState->root.fn->setSize(&layerState->root,
                                     layerRect.width,
                                     layerRect.height);
#endif
    }
#endif

#if LE_STREAMING_ENABLED == 1
    // there is an active stream in progress, service that to completion
    // before painting anything else
    if(_state.activeStream != NULL)
    {
        if(_state.activeStream->isDone(_state.activeStream) == LE_TRUE)
        {
            _state.activeStream = NULL;
        }
        else
        {
            _state.activeStream->exec(_state.activeStream);

            return LE_SUCCESS;
        }
    }
#endif

    updateWidgets(dt);

    leRenderer_Paint();

    return LE_SUCCESS;
}

uint32_t leLayerCount(void)
{
    if(_initialized == LE_FALSE)
        return 0;

    return _state.layerList.size;
}

int32_t leAddLayer(void)
{
    leLayerState* layer;
    leWidget* root;
    leSize disp;
    int32_t idx = _state.layerList.size;

    if(_initialized == LE_FALSE)
        return LE_FAILURE;

    layer = LE_MALLOC(sizeof(struct leLayerState));

    LE_ASSERT(layer != NULL);

    _leRenderer_CreateLayerState(layer);

    leList_PushBack(&_state.layerList,
                    layer);
```

```text
==== GFXC_GetPixelBuffer + GFXC_BlitBuffer (the render seam) ====
gfxPixelBuffer * GFXC_GetPixelBuffer(int32_t idx)
{
    return &canvas[baseCanvasID + activeCanvasID].pixelBuffer;
}

static gfxResult GFXC_BufferBlit(const gfxPixelBuffer* source,
                            const gfxRect* rectSrc,
                            const gfxPixelBuffer* dest,
                            const gfxRect* rectDest)
{
    void* srcPtr;
    void* destPtr;
    uint32_t row, rowSize;
    unsigned int width, height;
    gfxResult res = GFX_FAILURE;

#if (CONFIG_CANVAS_GPU_BLIT_ENABLE == true)
    res = gfxcGPU->blitBuffer(source,
                              rectSrc,
                              dest,
                              rectDest);
#endif

    if (res != GFX_SUCCESS)
    {
        width = (rectSrc->width < rectDest->width) ?
                    rectSrc->width : rectDest->width;
        height = (rectSrc->height < rectDest->height) ?
                    rectSrc->height : rectDest->height;
        rowSize = width * gfxColorInfoTable[dest->mode].size;

        for(row = 0; row < height; row++)
        {
            srcPtr = gfxPixelBufferOffsetGet(source, rectSrc->x, rectSrc->y + row);
            destPtr = gfxPixelBufferOffsetGet(dest, rectDest->x, rectDest->y + row);

            memcpy(destPtr, srcPtr, rowSize);
        }
    }

    return GFX_SUCCESS;
}

gfxResult GFXC_BlitBuffer(int32_t x,
                          int32_t y,
                          gfxPixelBuffer* buf)
{
    gfxRect srcRect, destRect;

	if (gfxcState != GFXC_RUNNING)
	{
		return GFX_FAILURE;
	}

	srcRect.x = 0;
    srcRect.y = 0;
    srcRect.height = buf->size.height;
    srcRect.width = buf->size.width;

    destRect.x = x;
    destRect.y = y;
    destRect.height = buf->size.height;
    destRect.width = buf->size.width;

	GFXC_BufferBlit(buf,
					&srcRect,
					&canvas[baseCanvasID + activeCanvasID].pixelBuffer,
					&destRect);


    return GFX_SUCCESS;
}

GFXC_RESULT _gfxcCopyBuffer(unsigned int srcID,
                         unsigned int destID,
                         const gfxRect * srcRect,
                         const gfxRect * destRect)
{
#if (CONFIG_CANVAS_GPU_BLIT_ENABLE == false)
    void* srcPtr;
    void* destPtr;
    uint32_t row, rowSize;
#endif

    if (canvas[srcID].pixelBuffer.mode != canvas[destID].pixelBuffer.mode ||
            srcRect->height != destRect->height ||
            srcRect->width != destRect->width)
        return GFX_FAILURE;

#if (CONFIG_CANVAS_GPU_BLIT_ENABLE == true)
    return gfxcGPU->blitBuffer(&canvas[srcID].pixelBuffer,
                       srcRect,
                       &canvas[destID].pixelBuffer,
                       destRect);
#else
    rowSize = canvas[srcID].pixelBuffer.size.width *
              gfxColorInfoTable[canvas[srcID].pixelBuffer.mode].size;

    for(row = 0; row < canvas[srcID].pixelBuffer.size.height; row++)
    {
        srcPtr = gfxPixelBufferOffsetGet(&canvas[srcID].pixelBuffer,
                                          srcRect->x, srcRect->y + row);
        destPtr = gfxPixelBufferOffsetGet(&canvas[destID].pixelBuffer,
                                          destRect->x, destRect->y + row);

        memcpy(destPtr, srcPtr, rowSize);
    }

    return GFX_SUCCESS;
#endif
}

GFXC_RESULT _gfxcSetBaseCanvasID(uint32_t base)
{
    if (baseCanvasID >= CONFIG_CANVAS_NUM_OBJ)
        return GFX_FAILURE;

    baseCanvasID = base;

    return GFX_SUCCESS;
}

gfxResult GFXC_GetLayerState(uint32_t idx, gfxLayerState* st)
{
    st->rect.x = canvas[baseCanvasID + idx].layer.pos.xpos;
    st->rect.y = canvas[baseCanvasID + idx].layer.pos.ypos;
    st->rect.width = canvas[baseCanvasID + idx].layer.size.width;
    st->rect.height = canvas[baseCanvasID + idx].layer.size.height;
    st->enabled = canvas[baseCanvasID + idx].active;

    return GFX_SUCCESS;
}
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-26 13:10:22Z)**_

I prototyped Path B far enough to hit its real wall, and it changed my recommendation. Here's what I found:

**Your off-screen intuition is correct about *tearing*.** `s_fb_nav` is single-buffered, Legato renders into it via the vendor `GFXC_BlitBuffer` seam, and the LCDC composites it on OVR1. Our overdraw would write the same buffer the same way Legato already does — corners are tiny and drawn on damage, not per-scan — so no partial-scan artifact. That part's fine.

**But the glitch risk in B isn't tearing — it's *timing*, and it's worse than I flagged:**

1. **No vendor-legal post-paint hook.** `leUpdate()` → `leRenderer_Paint()` runs inside a generated FreeRTOS task ([le_gen_harmony.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/gfx/legato/generated/le_gen_harmony.c) / [tasks.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/tasks.c)) — all under `config/default`. Legato exposes **no "paint complete" callback**; the canvas callback ([gfx_canvas.c:470](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/gfx/canvas/gfx_canvas.c#L470)) fires only on fade/move effects. So to run "right after paint" we'd need our own side-task racing the Legato task.

2. **Damage repaint clobbers us.** Legato repaints only damaged sub-rects. Every highlight swap / press repaints that button's corners *hard* via the vendor skin — erasing our previous smoothing until the side-task re-runs. That's a visible **1-frame hard-corner flash** on every interaction. A real glitch, just not a tearing one.

3. **Doesn't generalize.** You said buttons across the UI vary in size/color but share the radius. B would need a per-layer post-paint pass on BASE (dashboard) and OVR2 (dialogs) too, each enumerating buttons with their own colors — far more than a nav touch-up.

**Meanwhile, Path A has a much lighter variant than I described** — I was wrong that it forces a pipeline fork. With dynamic vtables on, I can **capture the original `_paint` pointer and wrap it**:

```c
extern leButtonWidgetVTable buttonWidgetVTable;
static leWidget_DrawFunction_FnPtr s_orig_paint;   // captured at init

static void marvin_button_paint(leButtonWidget* b) {
    s_orig_paint((leWidget*)b);                     // vendor draws bg+label+border (hard corners)
    if (b->widget.status.drawState == LE_WIDGET_DRAW_STATE_DONE &&
        b->widget.style.cornerRadius == NAV_CORNER_RADIUS)
        aa_corners(b);                              // overdraw 4 corners via leRenderer_BlendPixel
}
```

No reimplementation of the paint state machine — we let the vendor paint run to `DONE`, then blend the corner band with `leRenderer_BlendPixel` (coverage as alpha; no even GetPixel/Lerp needed). It runs **inside the paint pass**, so there's **zero timing window** — damage→repaint→AA in one pass — and it covers **every** button app-wide with one ~40-line file in our tree.

Net cost of A: one MCC config flag (`LE_DYNAMIC_VTABLES`, regen-safe, allowed) + ~40 lines in `ui/`. RAM-only (vtables to BSS, no heap), no fork, no timing glitch.

So having actually traced B, I'd flip back to **A (wrapper variant)** — it's both cleaner *and* lighter than B, and it's the only one that's glitch-free by construction and generalizes to all your buttons.

Want me to plan A out concretely (the MCC flag change, where the init hook lands, and the `aa_corners` helper), or do you want to weigh the `LE_DYNAMIC_VTABLES` global flag first?

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-26 13:12:36Z)**_

Correct — let me state the scope precisely, then verify the one thing the whole plan hinges on (that `LE_DYNAMIC_VTABLES` is a real MCC toggle, not a hand-edit).

**Scope clarification:** The wrapper `_paint` is installed for the button *type*, so it runs for every button — but the AA overdraw is **gated on `cornerRadius > 0`**. So:
- Buttons with rounded corners (your nav + anything with radius set) → AA corners.
- Square buttons (`cornerRadius == 0`) → pass straight through the vendor paint, untouched (cost = one integer check).

So it's "all *rounded* buttons get AA," and square ones are unaffected. Since you set radius deliberately, that's exactly the set you want.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-26 13:17:25Z)**_

This resolves the blocker — and the verified approach is actually cleaner than what we discussed. Let me confirm the dispatch chain I just traced and then answer your question:

**Dispatch is fully per-instance.** The renderer paints via `widget->fn->_handleEvent` → `_this->fn->_paint(_this)` ([legato_widget.c:1609](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/gfx/legato/widget/legato_widget.c#L1609)), and `fn` is a **writable per-instance pointer** (`const leWidgetVTable* fn` — pointer-to-const, but the pointer member itself is mutable; [legato_widget.h:626](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/gfx/legato/widget/legato_widget.h#L626)).

So we **don't need `LE_DYNAMIC_VTABLES` at all.** We make our own static copy of the button vtable in marvin's tree, override just `_paint`, and re-point the `fn` of whichever buttons we choose at our copy. No config flag, no generated-file edits, no app-wide RAM shift — and it's *scoped to exactly the buttons we re-point*.

**Your question — does this hit all buttons?** That's now a choice, not forced:
- The vtable copy + `_paint` override is shared (one struct), but it only applies to buttons whose `fn` we re-point.
- The overdraw is also gated on `cornerRadius > 0`, so even re-pointed square buttons are untouched.

So we can do **all rounded buttons app-wide** (re-point every button after each screen builds) or **nav-only first** (re-point just the 6 nav buttons, prove it, expand later). Given you said app-wide AA is "probably ok," I'd recommend **nav-first as the proving ground, then a one-line helper we call from each screen's init to extend app-wide** — same code, just more call sites.

Let me write this up as a proper plan.

```text
==== nav.c button enumeration + highlight (scheme swap) ====
static leButtonWidget *nav_button(unsigned int i)
{
    switch (i)
    {
        case 0:  return Navigation_BUTTON_NAV_DASHBOARD;
        case 1:  return Navigation_BUTTON_NAV_LOGS;
        case 2:  return Navigation_BUTTON_NAV_PERFORMANCE;
        case 3:  return Navigation_BUTTON_NAV_SYSTEM_INFO;
        case 4:  return Navigation_BUTTON_NAV_DIAGNOSTICS;
        default: return Navigation_BUTTON_NAV_SETTINGS;
    }
}

static void nav_close(void);   /* forward decl — nav_on_release may close the drawer */

/* Single-active highlight: paint the active entry selected, the rest unselected. */
static void nav_highlight(leButtonWidget *active)
{
    unsigned int i;

    for (i = 0u; i < NAV_COUNT; i++)
    {
        leButtonWidget *b = nav_button(i);
        b->fn->setScheme(b, (b == active) ? &SCHEME_NAV_BUTTON_SELECTED
                                          : &SCHEME_NAV_BUTTON_UNSELECTED);
    }
}

/* Released-event sink for every nav entry. Switch the highlight; Dashboard means
 * "back to the main view" so it also closes the drawer, while the other entries
 * just change the selection and stay open. The active screen-switch will hook
 * here once the per-screen canvas model lands. */
static void nav_on_release(leButtonWidget *btn)
{
    nav_highlight(btn);

    if (btn == Navigation_BUTTON_NAV_DASHBOARD)
    {
        nav_close();
    }
}

static void nav_buttons_init(void)
{
    unsigned int i;

    /* Route every nav-entry release through nav_on_release (runtime-registered
     * here — the Navigation screen wires no button events itself) and round the
     * corners (not an MGS option). */
    for (i = 0u; i < NAV_COUNT; i++)
    {
        nav_button(i)->fn->setReleasedEventCallback(nav_button(i), nav_on_release);
        nav_button(i)->fn->setCornerRadius(nav_button(i), NAV_CORNER_RADIUS);
    }

    /* Dashboard is the active entry at startup — set the highlight only (calling
     * the release sink here would close the not-yet-open drawer). */
```

```md
# Plan: anti-aliased rounded button corners (marvin UI)

## Context

marvin's nav-drawer buttons use the Legato classic skin's rounded-rect fill
(`cornerRadius` set in code via `setCornerRadius`). That fill draws the four
corners with `leRenderer_ArcFill` (Bresenham), which has **hard, stepped edges —
no anti-aliasing**. This is the deferred cosmetic item in
`firmware/marvin/docs/ui_compositor.md` §10. The goal is smooth (AA) corners on
the nav buttons, implemented entirely in marvin's own source tree.

### Why this approach (and what we ruled out)

- **Editing the Legato skin** (`legato_widget_skin_classic_common.c`) — the
  obvious place, but it's vendor/MCC code under `config/default/`. Forbidden by
  the new CLAUDE.md rule (regeneration silently overwrites; modified vendor files
  are invisible as customizations). An earlier attempt here was reverted.
- **`LE_DYNAMIC_VTABLES` + global `_paint` override** — would work, but the flag
  is **not** an MCC-exposed knob and is a plain unguarded `#define ... 0` in the
  generated `legato_config.h` (can't flip via config+regen, can't `-D`-override,
  can't hand-edit a generated file). Dead end under the rule.
- **Post-render overdraw on the nav canvas (Path B)** — no vendor-legal
  post-paint hook exists (`leUpdate` runs in a generated FreeRTOS task), and
  Legato's damage-driven repaint re-draws hard corners on every highlight/press,
  so smoothing would need a side-task that reintroduces a 1-frame hard-corner
  flash. Timing-fragile; doesn't generalize.
- **Chosen — per-instance vtable re-point (Path A').** `leWidget.fn` is a
  *writable per-instance pointer* to a `const` vtable
  ([legato_widget.h:626](../../Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/gfx/legato/widget/legato_widget.h)).
  We make our own static copy of the button vtable in marvin's tree, override
  only `_paint`, and re-point the nav buttons' `fn` at our copy. The renderer
  dispatches paint via `widget->fn->_handleEvent` → `_this->fn->_paint(_this)`
  ([legato_widget.c:1609](../../Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/gfx/legato/widget/legato_widget.c)),
  so our `_paint` is called by construction — **in-pass, no timing window, no
  config flag, no generated-file edits, no app-wide RAM cost.** Scoped to exactly
  the buttons we re-point.

## Scope

**Nav buttons only**, for now. The mechanism is a one-line-per-button helper, so
extending to dashboard/dialog buttons later is purely adding call sites. The AA
overdraw is additionally gated on `cornerRadius > 0`, so re-pointed square
buttons would be untouched anyway.

## Design

### New module: `firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/button_aa.{c,h}`

Owns the vtable copy, the `_paint` wrapper, the AA-corner overdraw, and the
coverage mask. All in marvin's tree — zero vendor edits.

**Shared state (file-static):**
- `static leButtonWidgetVTable s_aa_vt;` — our writable copy of the button vtable
  (one shared copy; all nav buttons originally share the same vtable).
- `static void (*s_orig_paint)(leWidget*);` — captured original `_paint`.
- `static leBool s_vt_ready;` — lazy-init guard.
- `static uint8_t s_mask[R][R];` + `static leBool s_mask_ready;` — coverage table
  for the shared radius `R = NAV_CORNER_RADIUS` (12).

**`void ButtonAA_Enable(leButtonWidget* b)`** — public entry point:
1. On first call, lazily init the shared vtable copy from the live instance:
   `s_aa_vt = *b->fn; s_orig_paint = b->fn->_paint; s_aa_vt._paint = aa_paint;`
   and build the coverage mask (one-time `sqrtf` loop, same math as the reverted
   patch: `cov = clamp(R + 0.5 - dist_to_arc_center, 0, 1) * 255`).
2. Re-point this instance: `b->fn = &s_aa_vt; b->widget.fn = (void*)&s_aa_vt;`
   (the renderer dispatches through `widget.fn`; both kept consistent, matching
   how the vendor constructor sets them).

**`static void aa_paint(leWidget* w)`** — the wrapper:
1. `s_orig_paint(w);` — vendor draws background (hard corners) + label + border.
   This is preemption-safe: the renderer calls `aa_paint` repeatedly until
   `drawState == DONE`, and we just forward each call.
2. After it returns, if `w->status.drawState == LE_WIDGET_DRAW_STATE_DONE` **and**
   `((leButtonWidget*)w)->widget.style.cornerRadius == R`, call `aa_corners`.

**`static void aa_corners(leButtonWidget* b)`** — the overdraw:
- Get screen rect: `b->fn->rectToScreen(b, &rect)` (original copied pointer).
- Determine fill color the same way the skin's `drawBackground` does:
  up → `leScheme_GetRenderColor(scheme, LE_SCHM_BASE)`,
  pressed → `LE_SCHM_BACKGROUND` (mirror
  [legato_widget_button_skin_classic.c:349](../../Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/gfx/legato/widget/button/legato_widget_button_skin_classic.c)).
- For each of the 4 corners: sample the backdrop from the rect's **extreme corner
  pixel** (e.g. `leRenderer_GetPixel(rect.x, rect.y)` for upper-left) — that pixel
  lies outside the rounded shape, so the vendor fill left it as background. No
  caching, no before-paint sampling.
- For each transition pixel in the corner's `R×R` box (coverage strictly between
  0 and 255), write `leColorLerp(bg, fill, cov*100/255, leRenderer_CurrentColorMode())`
  via `leRenderer_PutPixel`. Mirror the mask across the other 3 corners by index.
- Honor cumulative alpha if relevant (use `b->fn->getCumulativeAlphaAmount` like
  the skin does), else 255.

Reused APIs (all public, in our tree): `leRenderer_GetPixel`/`PutPixel`
([legato_renderer.h](../../Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/gfx/legato/renderer/legato_renderer.h)),
`leColorLerp` ([legato_color.h:632](../../Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/gfx/legato/common/legato_color.h)),
`leRenderer_CurrentColorMode`, `leScheme_GetRenderColor`.

### Wiring: `firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/nav.c`

In `nav_buttons_init()` (already iterates the 6 buttons and sets `cornerRadius`),
add `ButtonAA_Enable(nav_button(i));` inside the existing loop. Include
`ui/button_aa.h`. No other call sites.

### Build

Add `ui/button_aa.c` to the source set. Confirm how `ui/*.c` are listed for the
MPLAB build — if globbed, nothing to do; if enumerated, add it (in marvin's own
project file, not generated config).

## Constraints honored

- **Static allocation only** — one vtable struct + one `R×R` mask in BSS; no
  malloc. (Consistent with `feedback_static_allocation`.)
- **No vendor/generated edits** — everything new lives under `src/ui/`.
- **Comments**: one-line "why" only; the rationale/alternatives live here and in
  the journal, per CLAUDE.md.

## Verification

1. Build marvin in MPLAB; confirm `button_aa.c` compiles and links (no `sqrtf`
   surprises — `math.h`, already used elsewhere).
2. Flash to the SAM9X75 Curiosity board; open the nav drawer (hamburger on the
   dashboard).
3. Visually confirm the six nav buttons have **smooth** rounded corners against
   the panel background, in both selected and unselected schemes (the highlight
   swap changes fill color — AA must track it since fill is read from the live
   scheme each paint).
4. Press/hold a nav entry: the pressed-state fill swap must also show AA corners
   (exercises the `LE_SCHM_BACKGROUND` path).
5. Slide the drawer in/out a few times: corners stay smooth, no fl icker or
   stale-corner artifacts (validates the in-pass timing — repaint→AA same pass).
6. Confirm non-nav buttons (dashboard hamburger) are visually unchanged
   (override is scoped to re-pointed instances only).

## Follow-ups (not in this change)

- Extend app-wide by calling `ButtonAA_Enable` from dashboard/dialog button init.
- Generalize the mask cache if a second distinct radius is ever introduced
  (currently asserts/skips radii != `R`).
- Update `ui_compositor.md` §10 to mark AA corners resolved (after it lands).
```

```text
    CAMERA_ENABLE_DEBUG=0
    # Place the Legato CPU-rendered scratch buffer in non-cached DDR (same section
    # as the XLCDC framebuffer). Works around an MGS gen gap: with "Cacheable
    # Frame Buffers" off, the framebuffer is non-cached but the Legato render
    # buffer (LE_NO_CACHE_ATTR) is left empty/cacheable, so the 2D-engine blit
    # reads stale CPU-cached pixels -> streaky bleed. The #ifndef guard in
    # legato_renderer.c lets this -D win, surviving MGS regen.
    "LE_NO_CACHE_ATTR=__attribute__((section(\".region_nocache\")))"
    # Fretboard link transport: default is FLEXCOM1 UART. Uncomment to route
    # the fretboard command/data over the 10BASE-T1S link (LAN8651) instead —

    MARVIN_FRETBOARD_TRANSPORT=1
```

```c
#include "ui/button_aa.h"

#include <math.h>

#include "gfx/legato/common/legato_color.h"
#include "gfx/legato/core/legato_scheme.h"
#include "gfx/legato/renderer/legato_renderer.h"
#include "gfx/legato/widget/legato_widget.h"

#define R  BUTTON_AA_RADIUS

/* One shared vtable copy + the captured original paint: every button shares the
 * same classic-skin vtable, so a single overridden copy serves all callers. */
static leButtonWidgetVTable s_aa_vt;
static void (*s_orig_paint)(leButtonWidget*);
static leBool s_vt_ready = LE_FALSE;

/* Corner coverage [0..255]: 255 inside the arc, 0 outside, fractional on the
 * 1px transition band. Quadrant for the upper-left corner; other corners mirror
 * by index. Arc centre is the inner corner of the R x R box at (R, R). */
static uint8_t s_mask[R][R];
static leBool s_mask_ready = LE_FALSE;

static void build_mask(void)
{
    unsigned int x, y;

    for (y = 0u; y < R; y++)
    {
        for (x = 0u; x < R; x++)
        {
            float dx  = (float)R - (float)x - 0.5f;
            float dy  = (float)R - (float)y - 0.5f;
            float d   = sqrtf(dx * dx + dy * dy);
            float cov = (float)R + 0.5f - d;

            if (cov < 0.0f) cov = 0.0f;
            if (cov > 1.0f) cov = 1.0f;

            s_mask[y][x] = (uint8_t)(cov * 255.0f + 0.5f);
        }
    }

    s_mask_ready = LE_TRUE;
}

/* Smooth one corner box. (ox, oy) is its top-left in screen space; (mx, my) map
 * a box pixel to its mask cell. bg is sampled from the box's outermost pixel,
 * which the rounded fill leaves untouched. Only transition pixels are written. */
static void blend_corner(int32_t ox, int32_t oy,
                         leColor fill, leColorMode mode,
                         leBool flip_x, leBool flip_y)
{
    leColor bg = leRenderer_GetPixel(flip_x ? ox + (int32_t)R - 1 : ox,
                                     flip_y ? oy + (int32_t)R - 1 : oy);
    unsigned int px, py;

    for (py = 0u; py < R; py++)
    {
        for (px = 0u; px < R; px++)
        {
            unsigned int mx = flip_x ? (R - 1u - px) : px;
            unsigned int my = flip_y ? (R - 1u - py) : py;
            uint8_t cov = s_mask[my][mx];

            if (cov != 0u && cov != 255u)
            {
                leColor c = leColorLerp(bg, fill, (uint32_t)cov * 100u / 255u, mode);
                leRenderer_PutPixel(ox + (int32_t)px, oy + (int32_t)py, c);
            }
        }
    }
}

static void aa_corners(leButtonWidget* btn)
{
    leRect rect;
    leColor fill;
    leColorMode mode;
    int32_t rx, ry, rw, rh;

    btn->fn->rectToScreen(btn, &rect);

    rx = rect.x;
    ry = rect.y;
    rw = rect.width;
    rh = rect.height;

    /* Match the skin: pressed fills with BACKGROUND, released with BASE. */
    fill = leScheme_GetRenderColor(btn->widget.scheme,
                                   (btn->state != LE_BUTTON_STATE_UP)
                                       ? LE_SCHM_BACKGROUND : LE_SCHM_BASE);
    mode = leRenderer_CurrentColorMode();

    blend_corner(rx,                  ry,                  fill, mode, LE_FALSE, LE_FALSE);
    blend_corner(rx + rw - (int32_t)R, ry,                 fill, mode, LE_TRUE,  LE_FALSE);
    blend_corner(rx,                  ry + rh - (int32_t)R, fill, mode, LE_FALSE, LE_TRUE);
    blend_corner(rx + rw - (int32_t)R, ry + rh - (int32_t)R, fill, mode, LE_TRUE,  LE_TRUE);
}

static void aa_paint(leButtonWidget* btn)
{
    s_orig_paint(btn);

    if (btn->widget.status.drawState == LE_WIDGET_DRAW_STATE_DONE &&
        btn->widget.style.cornerRadius == R)
    {
        aa_corners(btn);
    }
}

void ButtonAA_Enable(leButtonWidget* btn)
{
    if (!s_mask_ready)
        build_mask();

    if (!s_vt_ready)
    {
        s_aa_vt = *btn->fn;
        s_orig_paint = btn->fn->_paint;
        s_aa_vt._paint = aa_paint;
        s_vt_ready = LE_TRUE;
    }

    btn->fn = &s_aa_vt;
    btn->widget.fn = (const leWidgetVTable*)&s_aa_vt;
}

```

Both compile cleanly (`-Wall -Wextra`, exit 0). Implementation is complete and syntax-verified against the project's exact build flags.

## Summary

Implemented anti-aliased rounded button corners for the nav drawer, entirely in marvin's own source — **zero vendor/generated edits**.

**New module** [button_aa.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/button_aa.c) / [button_aa.h](firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/button_aa.h):
- `ButtonAA_Enable(btn)` makes one shared, writable copy of the button vtable, overrides only `_paint`, and re-points the button's `fn` / `widget.fn` at it. No `LE_DYNAMIC_VTABLES`, no config flag, no per-instance RAM.
- The wrapper `aa_paint` calls the original paint (vendor draws bg + label + border), then on `DONE` with `cornerRadius == 12` overdraws the four corners.
- `aa_corners` samples the backdrop from each corner's extreme pixel (left as background by the rounded fill), then blends the 1px transition band with a precomputed 12×12 coverage mask via `leColorLerp` + `leRenderer_PutPixel`. Fill color tracks the live scheme (BASE/BACKGROUND), so the selected/unselected highlight and pressed states stay correct.
- Static-only: one vtable struct + one 144-byte mask in BSS.

**Wiring:** one line in `nav_buttons_init()` ([nav.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/nav.c)) inside the existing loop; source added to [user.cmake](firmware/marvin/cmake/marvin/default/user.cmake).

**What I couldn't do here:** flash/run. Verification needs the board — open the nav drawer and confirm smooth corners across selected/unselected/pressed states and a few slide cycles (steps in the plan file).

Two notes:
- Per CLAUDE.md, I haven't committed — say the word when you want that.
- The journal/`ui_compositor.md` §10 still lists AA corners as deferred. I'll update those to reflect this landing once you've confirmed it looks right on the board (or now, if you'd prefer). Want me to make that doc update?

---

```text
199	## 10a. Anti-aliased rounded button corners
200	
201	The nav buttons use the widget `cornerRadius` (set in code — not exposed in MGS), but the
202	classic skin's rounded-rect fill draws corners with `leRenderer_ArcFill` (hard, stepped
203	edges). Smoothing is done **without touching Legato/MCC code** (`config/default/` is
204	off-limits), via a per-instance vtable re-point in `src/ui/button_aa.c`:
205	
206	- `leWidget.fn` is a writable per-instance pointer to a `const` vtable. `ButtonAA_Enable`
207	  makes one shared writable copy of the button vtable, overrides only `_paint`, and points
208	  the button's `fn`/`widget.fn` at it. No `LE_DYNAMIC_VTABLES` (not an MCC knob; unguarded
209	  `#define 0` in generated `legato_config.h`), no global RAM cost — scoped to re-pointed
210	  buttons.
211	- The wrapper runs the original paint (bg + label + border), then on `DONE` with the
212	  supported radius overdraws the four corners: sample the backdrop from each corner's
213	  extreme pixel (left untouched by the rounded fill), then blend a 1px transition band from
214	  a precomputed coverage mask via `leColorLerp` + `leRenderer_PutPixel`. Fill is read from
215	  the live scheme each paint, so highlight (selected/unselected) and pressed states track.
216	- Runs **in-pass** (damage → repaint → AA in one paint), so no timing/flicker window.
217	- Wired from `nav_buttons_init()`; currently nav-only. Extending app-wide is just calling
218	  `ButtonAA_Enable` from other screens' button init. Single radius (`BUTTON_AA_RADIUS`);
219	  other radii pass through unsmoothed.
```

```text
7	**UI architecture — nav drawer complete; song/mode-select dialog is the next UI step.** The canvas compositor + per-screen-module model is built and validated on hardware: `ui_manager` orchestrates screens (string table + `screenInit/Show`; the MGS screen state machine is disabled, worked around with the `compat/le_gen_init.h` stub), the dashboard is its own MGS Screen on BASE, and the nav drawer is its own MGS Screen (`Navigation`) re-hosted onto OVR1 — they coexist live (no active-screen gate; `leUpdate`/`leInput` cover all attached layers). `LE_LAYER_COUNT`=3 is pinned via the never-shown `LayerBudget` screen. **Nav drawer is feature-complete:** slides in/out via canvas Move FX (`NAV_CLOSED_X` dodges the window-clip row-wrap; mid-slide reversal cancels the in-flight move), single-active highlight (Dashboard closes, others switch), clean close, rounded buttons (no AA — known cosmetic limitation). Authoritative design + the window-clip/alignment gotchas in [`ui_compositor.md`](ui_compositor.md); decisions 2026-06-25. **Next:** author song/mode-select as its own MGS Screen, hosted by `ui_manager` on OVR2 as a modal (assign `canvas[2]` a buffer, re-host onto layer 2, dashboard live behind) — first coexist-with-live-background exercise; the re-host + slide mechanics are proven on the nav. Ties into the song_list widget below (the scrollable list goes inside that dialog). The earlier "parked surfaces aren't pickable / reveal-then-promote" framing is **superseded** (a state-machine artifact).
8	
9	**Song-select operator UI — scrollable list widget built & validated on hardware.** Custom Legato widget `ui/song_list.{h,c}` (a hand-written `leWidget` subclass) renders the SELECT SONG setlist (tier badge + bold title + dim artist + right-aligned duration), driven by a decoupled row-provider callback (no catalog dependency); drag-scroll with time-based kinetic inertia, tap-to-select. Bring-up via the `songlist` console command + a catalog-backed demo provider (`ui/song_list_demo.{c,h}`) — scroll/select/opaque-fill confirmed on hardware. **Bringing it up surfaced and fixed a real Legato/GFX2D cache-coherency bug** (see decision log 2026-06-24): the CPU-rendered scratch buffer was cacheable, so the 2D-engine blit leaked stale pixels through opaque widgets — fixed by placing the scratch in non-cached DDR. **Next:** author the full SELECT SONG screen in MGS (album art + catalog-fed metadata panel + difficulty/mode/Select), and the **tier / career-setlist data model** (the `tier` badge needs the deferred catalog tier column). Two upstream Microchip Legato/gfx bugs to file (decision log).

11	**Song catalog loader — built and committed; exercised on hardware via the `catalog`/`songlist` console commands.** New `game/catalog.{h,c}` maps the recognizer's `(setlist, index)` → human labels (title/artist/bpm/length) from `<card>/games/gh3-wii/songs.csv`, so the UI/high-score display shows names instead of `#4`. Flat **CSV** (decided over the spec's JSON for the same reasons `results` is CSV — no on-device tokenizer, `FF_FS_MAX_FILES=1`, static buffers, pandas/Excel-editable). The two CSV helpers were extracted out of `results.c` into a shared `util/csv.{h,c}` and the catalog reuses them. Lazy-loads once into a fixed `[GP_N_SONGS]` static cache (file closed after load), so lookups are O(n) in RAM and don't fight `results.csv` for the single FatFs handle. `catalog` console command (`reload` / `ls` / `<main|bonus> <index>`) validates the path against a checked-in seed catalog (`data/games/gh3-wii/songs.csv`). Columns: `setlist,index,title,artist,album,bpm,length_s,year,genre,difficulty`. `title`/`artist`/`album` are real, sourced from the `SONGS` table in `tools/fetch_gh3_cover_art.py` (incl. proper UTF-8 — *Héroes del Silencio*, *Mauvais Garçon*); that script gained a `--catalog` mode that also fills `year`/`genre` from MusicBrainz on a networked run. `bpm`/`length_s`/`difficulty` are reserved-but-blank (GH3 surfaces no per-song difficulty; the authentic signal is the career tier, deferred). Catalog is labels only: a missing/stale card degrades to "Unknown song" and never touches recognition (compile-time in flash). **Deferred:** the stale-catalog version warning — `export_c.py` doesn't emit `GP_METADATA_VERSION` yet (open item below). **Next SD consumer:** album-artwork pre-cache (spec §4.8.7) — directory structure is now locked (`art/{small,large}/<setlist>-<NN>.{jpg,png}`, one size-tier subdir per DDR cache), marvin decode side not yet built.

13	**T1S inter-node link — built and working (marvin ↔ guitar).** marvin is the PLCA **coordinator** (node 0) on a 10BASE-T1S bus (LAN8651 over FLEXCOM4 SPI); hand-authored stack in `default/src/net/t1s/`. It sends the actuator command over T1S to the `guitar` follower node (id 2), which actuates the Wii GPIOs (guitar G1+G2 proven). Followers announce presence via a heartbeat (ethertype `0x88B6`); the `t1s` and `nodes` console commands report link/credits/per-node presence. Transport is behind `MARVIN_FRETBOARD_TRANSPORT={UART,T1S}` (T1S default on the `t1s` branch). The `fretboard` node (id 1) firmware is now **written, T1S-only** (fretboard journal 2026-06-17): it streams its 17-byte frame to marvin **and** drives the `guitar` node directly — its on-device model infers the bitmask and sends it peer-to-peer to `02:..:02`. marvin's RX side needed no changes — `fretboard_link.c`'s T1S frame handler already parses the frame from node id 1 (`DETECTOR_ADC_FRETBOARD`) and the node-table + heartbeat-presence demux already cover it. **Next (marvin side):** **active-source arbitration** — both marvin (timing pipeline) and the fretboard now address the guitar (`02:..:02`), so marvin needs active-detector/active-guitar selection to ensure exactly one source drives at a time (the fretboard's SW0 is an interim manual arm; until then, don't run marvin's timing pipeline to the guitar while the fretboard is armed). Then fretboard hardware bring-up. PoDL is design-direction only. Detail in [`../../../docs/t1s-podl-link.md`](../../../docs/t1s-podl-link.md); decision log entry 2026-06-17.
```
