36	| 2026-06-25 | **Re-enabled GFX Canvas Move FX to animate the nav drawer slide (reverses the earlier "FX off, do our own" call).** The nav drawer now slides in/out by animating its OVR1 canvas window position via `gfxcStartEffectMove` (DEC ease-out), rather than snapping. With a concrete slide need this is the textbook canvas-move case (the doc flagged it as where canvas FX earns its weight); rolling our own would just duplicate the FX timer + `GFX_CANVAS_Task` we already have, and the FX timer only ticks during an active move (no steady cost). Open slides −off→0; entry taps switch the highlight (Dashboard also closes); a move-done callback (`nav_fx_done`) disables OVR1 when a close finishes. **Window-clip gotcha (cost a few iterations):** a canvas layer can't sit truly off-screen — the clip emulates negative X by shifting the source pointer + shrinking the window, but it first aligns X *down* to a multiple of 4 (`x &= ~0x3`, non-32bpp) and wraps a row once \|X\| hits the surface width, briefly flashing the panel's left columns; and the layer update busy-waits for the vsync latch, so that bad frame displays before the hide. Fix: slide to the furthest 4-aligned X with \|X\| < NAV_W (`NAV_CLOSED_X`, derived from NAV_W — not a magic number) so the final shown frame is an in-bounds edge sliver, then `nav_fx_done` disables the layer to clear it. | Canvas Move FX over a hand-rolled stepper because the machinery already exists (just was disabled) and it's purpose-built for sliding a layer window with easing; the earlier FX-off decision was speculative (pre-slide). The off-screen constant is derived + documented (points at the exact clip line) rather than hard-coded, accepting a documented coupling to the generated canvas clip — same class as the cache/scratch and HEO-blender couplings. Full decoupling (own the slide via direct XLCDC position stepping) is the fallback if the clip bites again. |
37	| 2026-06-25 | **UI architecture: disable the MGS screen state machine and let the app own screen orchestration, so panels coexist as live, independently-interactive LCDC layers — `ui_manager` + per-screen modules. Authoritative design in [`ui_compositor.md`](ui_compositor.md).** Confirmed in the Legato core that `_state.layerList` is global, `leUpdate` renders/updates **every** attached layer each frame, and `leInput` picks touch across **all** attached layers top-to-bottom — there is no "active screen" render/pick gate. The only thing enforcing one-screen-at-a-time was `le_gen_init.c`'s state machine (`legato_showScreen` tears down the outgoing tree). Turning it off (and working around the MGS dangling-`le_gen_init.h` bug with a `compat/` stub) means we attach multiple panels' roots to different layers and they're all live + interactive at once. **Model:** each panel is authored as its own MGS Screen used as a *widget-tree factory* (`screenInit_` builds, `screenShow_` attaches + raises its `OnShow` composition root); `leAddRootWidget`/`leRemoveRootWidget` re-host a root onto whatever layer we choose. Layers: dashboard=BASE/0, nav=OVR1/1 (resident → "same nav over every view" free), modal song/mode dialog=OVR2/2 (sized to the dialog so live dashboard telemetry shows around it); camera=HEO outside Legato. Two verbs — **coexist** (overlay-as-layer, background live) and **replace** (swap base view on layer 0) — chosen per interaction, both owned by `ui_manager`, so the choice is reversible. `compositor.c` is promoted to `ui_manager`; per-screen/overlay modules own only their widgets+wiring. **This supersedes the earlier "parked surfaces aren't pickable / reveal-then-promote" idea in the doc** — that was a symptom of the state machine, now removed. | Greg's call to author nav + dialogs as separate MGS Screens (cleaner than overlapping layers in one Screen) collided with Legato's one-active-screen model; the resolution was to drop that model entirely rather than fight it, which the global-layerList facts make safe. Disabling the state machine also removes MGS's per-screen switch baggage outright (deleted code, not dormant) and hands us `screenInit/Show` directly. Live-coexistence (vs. freeze) was required because some dashboard telemetry must keep updating under the nav/dialog (the camera already self-updates on HEO). Per-screen modules + a `ui_manager` orchestrator keep each panel's wiring local (composition-root-per-screen) while one top-level module owns the scarce layer budget — matching the MCC-isolation idiom (own files via `user.cmake`). 3 UI layers + camera is the hard ceiling. | 
38	| 2026-06-25 | **The GFX Canvas regen pushed FreeRTOS `heap_1` past 40 KB → silent boot hang (zero DBGU output); raised `configTOTAL_HEAP_SIZE` 40960 → 100000.** Symptom: after the canvas MCC commit (`ed54f37`), marvin produced no DBGU output at all — bisected to that commit (`8de7c64` working). Not the compositor (it was stashed), and not the XLCDC OVR setup (BASE/HEO use the identical `LCDC_ATTRE`/`WAIT_ATTRS_EQ(SIP)` pre-`Start` pattern that already works, so OVR is symmetric). Root cause: the canvas additions (the dynamic `GFX_CANVAS_Task` + extra OSAL/driver allocations on the 4-layer/canvas display path) tipped cumulative `pvPortMalloc` during `SYS_Initialize` past the 40 KB `heap_1`. Because `configUSE_MALLOC_FAILED_HOOK=1` and `vApplicationMallocFailedHook()` is the MCC default (`taskDISABLE_INTERRUPTS(); for(;;){}`), the failed alloc spun with IRQs off **before** `APP_Initialize`/`log_init` (initialization.c:499) ran → no banner, indistinguishable from a dead board. **Two durable follow-ups (both carried):** (1) the heap size is **not** in `FreeRTOS.yml` — it's a raw literal in the generated `FreeRTOSConfig.h`, so the bump is an **MCC re-apply patch** (joins patch #8, also a `FreeRTOSConfig.h` edit) and will silently revert on the next regen → hang returns; set it in the MCC FreeRTOS component if it exposes Total Heap Size, else keep it on the re-apply list. (2) Patch `vApplicationMallocFailedHook` **and** `vApplicationStackOverflowHook` to emit a marker before the spin — a one-line DBGU write would have turned this multi-step bisect into an instant diagnosis. | Same silent-spin footgun already flagged for `vApplicationStackOverflowHook` (Open questions), now confirmed to bite via the malloc path too — heap exhaustion and stack overflow both present as identical dead-board hangs with the stock hooks. `heap_1` (never frees) is correct for marvin's static-allocation discipline, but MCC tasks + Legato OSAL still need it, so its size is load-bearing and must be tracked. 100000 is generous (+60 KB) headroom for now; right-size later once boot logs `xPortGetFreeHeapSize()`. Found by Greg's heap hypothesis after the XLCDC poll-loop theory was ruled out by BASE/HEO symmetry. |
39	| 2026-06-25 | **`GFX_CANVAS_Task` runs at priority 2 (the UI band), set via the gfx_canvas component's Task Priority field — not the generated default of 1.** Band 2 is marvin's UI tier (`LEGATO`, `DRV_MAXTOUCH`, `XLCDC`, `SYS_INPUT`; see 2026-05-21 priority re-tiering); the canvas task joins it as a fifth member. Stack 1024 / 10 ms delay kept (matches the other MCC UI tasks; FX is off so it mostly idles between updates). | The canvas task commits Legato's rendered output to the hardware layers (`gfxcShowCanvas`/`CanvasUpdate`/bind) — it *is* a UI task, peer to `XLCDC_Tasks` and downstream of `LEGATO_Tasks`, so it belongs in the same band under the established rule "a late UI paint is jitter only → UI stays the lowest *active* band and yields to vision (4) and strum-critical (5)." The generated default of **1** is wrong twice over: band 1 is **reserved** (future housekeeping/watchdog), and it would sit an active critical-path task below its UI peers. Same band as Legato (not above) is correct — both are event/short-poll and mostly blocked, and canvas presentation operates on shared state asynchronously, so there's no producer/consumer inversion like the old VideoTask one. Set in the component yml (per the 2026-05-21 "MCC priorities live in yml" rule) so regen reproduces it with **no `tasks.c` re-apply patch**. The dynamic `xTaskCreate` (vs static) is unchanged — consistent with the other MCC tasks on heap_1; static conversion stays a separate carried item. |
40	| 2026-06-25 | **Operator-UI presentation layer = a marvin compositor over the GFX Canvas component: pre-render UI panels into static non-cached RAM surfaces, multiplex the two free LCDC overlay layers (`OVR1`/`OVR2`) across them. Design captured in [`ui_compositor.md`](ui_compositor.md).** The goal is to bring a panel up (or slide it in) instantly without re-rendering or redrawing what's behind it. Confirmed the enabling fact in code: Legato's only "where do I render" knob is the active layer's `pixelBuffer.pixels` (it paints a scratch buffer, then `DRV_XLCDC_BlitBuffer` copies into `drvLayer[activeLayer].pixelBuffer`); there is **no** stock Legato API to render a widget tree into an arbitrary off-screen buffer. **GFX Canvas is exactly that missing indirection** — `GFXC_GetPixelBuffer` hands Legato a canvas object's buffer and `gfxcSetBaseCanvasID` switches which canvas a layer renders into, with `gfxcSetLayer`/show/hide/position/alpha + fade/move on top. Layer budget: `BASE`=background, `OVR1`/`OVR2`=swappable overlays (to be enabled — `XLCDC_TOT_LAYERS` is 2 today), `HEO`=live camera (off-limits). Legato stays the **renderer** (fonts, `song_list`); a thin `ui/` compositor owns surface↔layer multiplexing. Touch handled by **reveal-then-promote** (parked surfaces are non-interactive; promote to a live Legato layer to interact). Phased plan P0–P5 + open questions in the doc. **Design only — no code/MCC yet.** | Reverses the earlier "back off canvas" — that call was made on the **wrong axis**: canvas was dismissed for the *slide animation* (which direct `XLCDC_SetLayerWindowXYPos` stepping handles fine, no framework needed), but the actual problem is the **off-screen surface pool** (render content decoupled from a hardware layer), and that is canvas's literal reason to exist. The two homegrown alternatives lose: DIY pixel-buffer retarget reimplements canvas's per-surface/scratch/binding bookkeeping (~half of canvas, growing once surfaces aren't full-screen); direct-layer-only can present/animate but can't get Legato content *into* a surface. Canvas's earlier objections are addressable, not fatal: it deletes the static `frame_buffer` array, but we *use* the canvas buffers as our surfaces (statically allocated, non-cached per the 2026-06-24 fix), so static-allocation holds; the dynamic `GFX_CANVAS_Task` converts to `xTaskCreateStatic` or rides alongside the existing MCC dynamic tasks. Binding constraint is **layers (2 free), not memory** (~21 MB free in the 32 MB `ram_nocache` after the ISC pool + scratch; full-screen RGB565 ≈ 2 MB, most overlays far less). Resolves spec Q5 for the *presentation* layer (Legato renderer + canvas compositor) without dictating per-screen authoring. |
41	| 2026-06-24 | **Legato CPU-render scratch buffer must live in non-cached DDR (`.region_nocache`) — fixed a GFX2D cache-coherency bleed; grew `ram_nocache` 16→32 MB.** Symptom (found during song-list bring-up): dashboard content streakily "bled through" an opaque overlay widget, intermittently, only where CPU-rendered text was. Active render path is **CPU software** (`leRenderer_FillArea` → `_RGBBlendFill`; glyphs too) into a **scratch buffer**, then **`DRV_GFX2D_Blit`** (the SAM9X75 2D engine) copies scratch→framebuffer. The framebuffer is non-cached (`FB_CACHE_NC` → `.region_nocache`) but the Legato scratch was **cacheable**: `LE_NO_CACHE_ATTR` was an empty no-op `#define` and `LE_COHERENT_ATTR = CACHE_ALIGN` (alignment only). The blit's `dcache_CleanInvalidateByAddr` of the cached scratch is insufficient on ARM926 → the 2D engine reads stale CPU-cached lines → streaky, cache-line-granularity bleed. **Fix:** define `LE_NO_CACHE_ATTR = __attribute__((section(".region_nocache")))` in **`user.cmake`** (the `#ifndef` guard in the generated `legato_renderer.c` lets the `-D` win → survives MGS regen, no generated-tree patch); MCC grew `ram_nocache` 16→32 MB to host it (ddram.ld + plib_mmu.c + `DDRAM_NO_CACHE_SIZE`). **Confirmed on hardware** (commits `d36640f` + `c0f316c`). **Two upstream Microchip Legato/gfx bugs to file:** (1) with "Cacheable Frame Buffers" **off**, the generator non-caches the framebuffer but leaves the Legato render scratch cacheable (`LE_NO_CACHE_ATTR` empty) — the gap that bit us; (2) `DRV_GFX2D_Fill` omits the `dcache_CleanInvalidateByAddr` that `DRV_GFX2D_Blit` has (latent — bites any GPU-fill config, e.g. `LE_WIDGET_BUFFER_ENABLE=1`). | Root-caused by elimination, not by reading (every software-logic path traced correct): a bare opaque magenta fill still bled, hiding the dashboard cleared it, and non-cached scratch fixed it → it's the cached-scratch ↔ 2D-engine coherency, below the software layer. Non-cached is the correct policy on this SoC — Microchip already chose it for the framebuffer (`FB_CACHE_NC`) rather than trusting cache maintenance for a DMA-/GPU-read buffer; the scratch is the same kind of buffer and should match. Adding cache maintenance to `DRV_GFX2D_Fill` would *not* fix this (Fill isn't on the path; the on-path `Blit` already invalidates and still leaked). System-wide rule for this board: any buffer the 2D engine or display DMA reads must be non-cached (or carry correct, sufficient maintenance — which the cacheable path here does not). |
42	| 2026-06-24 | **Song-select setlist = a hand-written custom Legato widget (`leWidget` subclass), not the stock list widget.** `ui/song_list.{h,c}`: subclass with overridden `_paint`/`update`/touch handlers. Stock `leListWidget` is disabled **and** its item model (icon + one string) can't render the tier-badge + two-line + right-aligned-duration row. Design: **row-provider callback** `songlist_row_fn` (widget never includes `game/catalog.h`; the screen owns catalog→row mapping + future tier grouping); **drag + kinetic inertia** computed from the **FreeRTOS tick** (`leUpdate(0)` means the framework `dt` is always 0, so the widget measures real elapsed time itself for frame-rate-independent motion); **tap-to-select** (<10 px movement) with a selection callback; **virtualized software paint** (`leRenderer_RectFill` + `leStringRenderer_DrawCString`, visible rows only, no per-row child widgets); single **pool allocation** with the vtable built by **copying the base vtable at runtime** (project builds `LE_DYNAMIC_VTABLES=0`, so `_leWidget_FillVTable` isn't linkable and the GenerateVTable path is compiled out); declared **opaque** (`BACKGROUND_FILL`) so Legato composites it. Lives entirely in `ui/` (added via `user.cmake`) — zero edits to the generated `gfx/legato/` tree. Bring-up: `ui/song_list_demo.{c,h}` + a `songlist` console command (`attach`/`off`/`hide`/`show`/`solid`/`tree`/`stats`) with a catalog-backed provider; **validated on hardware**. | Matches the project's MCC-isolation idiom (own module + `user.cmake`, like `console`/`perf_log`); the widget is the primary, reusable piece, so it was built first, ahead of the MGS screen around it. Row-provider keeps the widget generic and testable and lets the screen map `Catalog_At(i)` → row (and supply tier badges once the tier column exists). Pool allocation (not static) because Legato recursively `LE_FREE`s the whole child tree on screen teardown (`legato_widget.c`) — a static widget attached to a screen would feed a static pointer to `LE_FREE`; the Legato widget pool is the accepted heap carve-out, and the widget is one self-contained allocation (fixed internal scratch, no secondary mallocs). Time-based inertia (vs per-tick) because the update cadence is render-bound (~55 Hz) and irregular under the priority-2 UI task. Tier badges blank until the deferred catalog `tier` column lands. |

The macOS worry ("all 4 FT4232H channels show as serial ports, need to swap a driver") turned out to be a non-issue: Apple's in-kernel FTDI driver binds all four as `/dev/cu.usbserial-*`, but libusb still claims channel A for MPSSE — `libusb_claim_interface(0)` succeeds and OpenOCD only logs a harmless `libusb_detach_kernel_driver ... LIBUSB_ERROR_ACCESS` warning before proceeding. On Apple Silicon Tahoe the driver can't be `kextunload`ed anyway, and no EEPROM reflash is required. nTRST/nSRST aren't wired into the MPSSE byte layout, so reset lines aren't driven — halt/resume work over JTAG regardless; revisit if flash/reset-halt needs them. Note: OpenOCD must be run *outside* the Claude Code command sandbox — the sandbox blocks libusb USB enumeration (libusb sees 0 devices), which produced misleading "device not found" errors until diagnosed. |
60	| 2026-06-08 | **Fretboard link moves USB CDC host → direct FLEXCOM2 USART** (`actuator/fretboard_link.c`). The SAM9X75 Curiosity *Hybrid* board (new target, MCC ported in `598d370`/`3af09bc`) has no host-capable USB port, so the EDBG-CDC-bridge transport is gone. marvin now talks UART directly to the fretboard's SERCOM1: `PA13` FLEXCOM2_IO0 (TX) / `PA14` FLEXCOM2_IO1 (RX) ↔ fretboard `PB01` RX / `PB00` TX, 500 000 Bd 8N1. FLEXCOM2 regenerated in **ring-buffer mode** (RX ring 512 B, TX ring 64 B). The public `FretboardLink_{Initialize,Send,IsConnected}` API and all perf-log records (FBL_SEND/CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE stamps, ACTUATOR, FRETBOARD_RAW) are unchanged, so `timing_pipeline`/`manual_control` and host `marvin-perf` need no edits. | The link is unchanged at the fretboard end (always SERCOM1 UART @ 500 000); only marvin's side was USB-bridged. Ring-buffer mode chosen over the basic single-transfer plib because the fretboard streams 17-byte frames continuously at 240 Hz: the basic plib disables RXRDY between a completed Read and the next arm, risking overrun, whereas the ring fills from its own ISR with no gap. RX is now a simple drain — a persistent read-threshold (`DS_FRAME_LEN`) notification wakes `fretboard_rx_task`, which pulls bytes off the ring and runs the same `0x03 … 0xFC` resync as before; the separate `s_rx_stream` stream buffer + ISR re-arm are deleted (the ring *is* the buffer). TX drops the USB Write/ack-semaphore dance: a ring-buffer `Write` copies the byte and returns, so "ack" is the enqueue instant. No enumeration/attach/detach → `s_connected` becomes a static `s_link_up`. The `CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE` perf-stage name is now historical (it's a UART enqueue) but kept to avoid a host-decoder schema change. |

VTABLES isn't an MCC knob and is an unguarded #define 0 in generated
config; a post-render overdraw has no vendor-legal hook and fights
damage-repaint. The per-instance re-point exploits leWidget.fn being a
writable pointer to a const vtable: no config flag, one vtable + mask in
BSS, runs in-pass (no timing window), scoped to re-pointed buttons.

config/default/. Design notes in ui_compositor.md §10a; journal updated.

Syntax-checked with the project's XC32 flags; on-hardware check pending.

EOF
echo "=== result ===" && git log --oneline -1 && git status --short
